name: Extreme C ch. 5 cache-friendly row-major matrix summation
listed_description: Example program that sums a large integer matrix either row by row (cache-friendly) or column by column (cache-unfriendly) to show the effect of cache locality.
claim_text: Row-major summation of a 20,000 by 20,000 matrix took about 5.2 s against about 15.4 s for column-major; the book calls the gap about 10 seconds.
book_benchmark: Shell time of the compiled example on 20,000 x 20,000 ints, friendly-sum vs not-friendly-sum, built with clang on macOS, no optimization flags stated, CPU not stated; single run each, includes matrix fill and allocation.
found_in: book: Extreme C (2019), ch. 5 Stack and Heap, section Performant environments / Caching (example 5.6)

name: dlmalloc
listed_description: Doug Lea's general-purpose memory allocator, named by the book as an alternative to the default C library malloc and free.
claim_text: Book only lists it among allocators other than the default C library ones and suggests readers try them; no numbers.
found_in: book: Extreme C (2019), ch. 5 Stack and Heap, section Performant environments / Allocation and deallocation cost

name: ptmalloc
listed_description: Multi-thread-aware allocator derived from dlmalloc (the basis of glibc malloc), named by the book among C allocator libraries other than the default.
claim_text: Book only lists it among alternative allocator libraries; no numbers.
guessed_baseline: single-lock dlmalloc / default C library malloc
found_in: book: Extreme C (2019), ch. 5 Stack and Heap, section Performant environments / Allocation and deallocation cost

name: Fixed-size memory pool (preallocated block pool)
listed_description: Technique of preallocating a pool of fixed-size heap blocks handed out through an acquire and release API, to cut the number of malloc and free calls.
claim_text: Book says a preallocated fixed-size block pool reduces allocations and gains some performance, and gives deterministic behavior; qualitative only.
found_in: book: Extreme C (2019), ch. 5 Stack and Heap, section Performant environments / Memory pools
